status: Secondary spatial-locality application designed after the whole-code thermodynamic benchmark. Frozen, not an independent archive or a revision of previous gates. No new configurations, trajectories or test rows.
reference: Lenggenhager, Gökmen, Ringel, Huber and Koch-Janusz, Optimal Renormalization Group Transformation from Information Theory, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.10.011037 . The theorem concerns perfect RSMI coarse-graining. The measured codes are not known to be perfect. A finite empirical directional prediction test neither invokes that theorem as proof nor establishes the range of the thermodynamic Hamiltonian.
inputs: Frozen published code maps: rsmi, species-A corner bits, kmeans_A_dipole and composition. Index 9,8,0 archive; 10240 native train and 2048 native validation parents per beta. No beta 6. For each parent and each of the eight offsets of the nonoverlapping 2-cube partition, analyze all 1000 coarse sites. For the origin-zero partition compare the RSMI output to the exact public 250-byte validation encoding.
geometry: At each coarse site H, N is its full ordered six axial nearest-neighbor 4-symbol vector (up to 4096 values). F is ONE axial coarse site two tile steps away, with direction J uniform over six signed axes and supplied to the predictor. Join H,N,F on the same parent with periodic boundaries. Report I(H;N) and I(H;F|N,J), never multiply the latter by six or call it joint exterior MI. Near conditioning is on the same six-tuple for all J. It does not include diagonal neighbors.
fit: One conventional conditional table per temperature and map fitted to that temperature's TRAIN rows, with fixed shrinkage toward the neighboring predictor: marginal 0.5 counts per label, near table prior 16 times fitted marginal, farther table prior 128 times near forecast. The physical map, hyperparameters, practical thresholds and estimand transfer unchanged; conditional lookup tables do not transfer. This asks what local law a representation admits at each temperature, not if interactions are temperature independent.
bracket: On validation parents, plug-in Hhat(H|N) - crossentropy(q_F) is a lower-score estimator in expectation of the conditional information. crossentropy(q_N) - plug-in Hhat(H|N,F,J) is an upper-score estimator in expectation, since conditional entropy is concave and held-out cross entropy bounds the true conditional entropy from above. Same construction for I(H;N) with marginal and near. Report both, raw plug-in difference and held-out log-score gain. These are bracket endpoint estimators, not samplewise population bounds; the latter score difference alone cannot establish conditional MI. No assumption that the farther observable is conditionally independent.
uncertainty: Delete one of 32 disjoint equally sized validation parent packets from the pooled table. Student-jackknife pointwise 95% sampling intervals, conditional on independent trained tables; not rigorous distribution-free coverage or refit uncertainty. Finite-sample entropy bias deliberately remains in the conservative directions. Cross-method comparisons descriptive and labels' marginal entropies reported; a collapsed or less informative code is not automatically more physical.
primary: For the warm beta 2.7111 RSMI code, the lower 95% endpoint for accessible near information must exceed 0.02 nats AND the upper 95% endpoint for extra information from a single registered farther tile at fixed N must be below 0.01 nats. Intersection gate, both required. Zero/hot and cold descriptive. Even success demonstrates a finite geometry with weak residual dependence and useful near correlations, not RSMI uniqueness, exact Markov locality or an RG fixed point.
controls: Analytical relabeling of actual tables F=H and F=constant, conditional empirical MI exactly Hhat(H|N) and zero, check estimators surround the empirical value to arithmetic tolerance. No scientific conclusions from the planted channels. Inspect resulting parent-group intervals and comparator controls.
